newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia faces average to wet weather-Bureau.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia faces average to wet weather-Bureau.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Meteorology said on Tuesday the outlook for rainfall patterns across Australia for the three months to January 1997 indicated average or wetter than normal conditions.

Districts with a significant chance of being wetter than average include western parts of Victoria, central and southern tablelands and slopes of New South Wales, northern Tasmania and northern parts of Queensland.
Other states have a high chance of average rainfall with some isolated districts falling in the wetter than normal category, it said.
The predictions are based on Southern Oscillation Index (SOI) trends and recent rainfall patterns, it said.
The SOI value for October was +4, continuing the pattern of small positive values observed throughout the year, it said.
Ocean temperatures in the eastern Pacific Ocean continue to be slightly cooler than average, particularly in the depths of the ocean, it said.
Statistical models and current conditions continue to suggest significant rainfall early in the wet season this year in tropical northern Australia, it said.
Rainfall in northern Australia during October was above average, particularly in Queensland, it said.
Tropical trade winds were also stronger than normal during October, feeding in moisture for the early wet season, it said.
Warm sea surface temperatures north of Australia coupled with current positive SOI values were generally indicative of above average rainfall early in the wet season, it said.
These conditions also favour a slight increase in the number of tropical cyclones over Australian region waters during the season, it said.
